Bridge reads an NFC tag you hold the phone to when your server asks, and sends what the tag contains to the server URL you configure.
Bridge lists your upcoming calendar events when your server asks, and sends them only to the server URL you configure.
Bridge opens the camera on screen when your server asks for a photo or a barcode scan. You see what the camera sees the whole time, and you take photos yourself.
Bridge looks up a contact's name, phone numbers and emails when your server asks, and sends at most 20 matches to the server URL you configure.
Bridge reads your health data (heart rate, HRV, sleep, workouts, steps…) and sends it only to the server URL you configure.
Bridge lists and controls the accessories already set up in Apple's Home app when your server asks, while the app is open. Unlocking, opening a garage door or disarming always asks you first.
Bridge uses significant location changes to wake up and check your server for jobs, and reports a one-shot location when the server asks. No continuous GPS.
Bridge reports your current location to your server when it asks.
Bridge records a short voice clip when your server asks, while the app is open (iOS shows the orange dot). The clip goes only to the server URL you configure.
Bridge reports today's steps, distance and floors, and barometer readings, to your server when it asks.
Bridge sends small, downscaled copies of your most recent photos to your server when it asks. Full-resolution images never leave the phone.
Bridge lists and adds reminders when your server asks, and sends them only to the server URL you configure.
Bridge turns a voice clip it just recorded into text, on the phone when possible, and sends the text only to the server URL you configure.
